stories.headline: Gold edges back above $4,000 after a 4% weekly fall

impacts.why: FXStreet: a softer dollar helped, but inflation-driven Fed hike bets cap gold's upside; resistance near $4,100.
Reuters: gold fell more than 4% last week before steadying near $4,001.

stories.meaning: Your gold ETC (SGLN) follows the gold price, which has had a rough few weeks as markets bet on more US rate rises. It steadied on Monday, but FXStreet sees resistance near $4,100, and Wednesday's Fed decision is the next big test.

priced_in.note: A Fed hold is fully priced; the December hike odds (about 80%, Reuters) are what move gold.

sources.title: Gold rebounds from three-month low, holds $4,000 as FOMC looms
Asian shares make cautious start, Brent eases from six-month high

stories.summary: Gold rose modestly from Friday's three-month low to just above $4,000 an ounce in Asia on Monday, after falling more than 4% last week. FXStreet credits a softer dollar and lower bond yields, while strong US data and Fed hike bets limit the upside ahead of Wednesday's Fed meeting.

explainer.meaning: spreading the cost of equipment over the years it is expected to be useful; a longer life means smaller yearly costs and higher reported profits

stories.headline: Huang says Nvidia GPUs last eight-plus years and are a low-risk asset for lenders

impacts.why: Yahoo Finance: Huang says lender risk on Nvidia compute is low; Burry argues the financing plan could hide risks in private credit.

stories.meaning: A worry hanging over Nvidia, in your Mag7 pie, is whether the companies buying its chips with borrowed money can keep paying. Huang argues the chips hold their value for longer than lenders assume, which would make that borrowing safer. Critics like Burry disagree, and AP says high borrowing costs for AI loans are a concern for markets this week.

priced_in.note: Nvidia fell 0.59% on Friday (TechFlow); the AI-financing debate has weighed on chip shares this month.

sources.title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia GPUs could last over 8 years, not 4, carry 'really high' residual value

stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told Yahoo Finance at GTC Berlin that its AI systems stay useful for eight years or more, not the four-year cycle lenders often assume, and carry high residual value. AI cloud firms such as CoreWeave have borrowed billions against Nvidia GPUs. Investor Michael Burry has called Nvidia's AI-financing push a 'Wall Street stunt'.

explainer.meaning: contracts that trade before the market opens and hint at which way shares will start the day

stories.headline: Asian shares start the week cautiously after the S&P 500's second weekly loss

impacts.why: AP: S&P 500 down 0.5% Friday for a second weekly loss; Reuters: US futures +0.2% Monday.

stories.meaning: Your Vanguard All-World fund (VWRP) is about 60% US shares, so last week's US losses pulled it down and it is now 3.7% below its 6 Oct high. Monday started quietly, with traders waiting for big tech results and Wednesday's Fed decision.

priced_in.note: Futures only edged up 0.2% (Reuters) as markets wait for earnings and the Fed.

sources.title: Shares fall in Asia after a decline on Wall Street, and oil prices fall more than 1%
Asian shares make cautious start, Brent eases from six-month high

stories.summary: Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi slipped on Monday while US stock futures edged up about 0.2%. On Friday the S&P 500 fell 0.5% for a second straight weekly loss, the Dow 1.2% and the Nasdaq 0.2%. AP says investors want proof this week that heavy AI spending will pay off.

explainer.meaning: the main global benchmark price for oil, used to price most of the world's crude

stories.headline: Brent oil eases from a four-year high as Trump holds off on new Iran strikes
stories.meaning: Oil above $110 keeps inflation high, which is why central banks are talking about raising rates. A small dip on Monday doesn't change the picture: sources say supply through the Strait of Hormuz is still disrupted.

priced_in.note: Brent rose from under $97 in early October (AP).

sources.title: Asian shares make cautious start, Brent eases from six-month high
Shares fall in Asia after a decline on Wall Street, and oil prices fall more than 1%
US Stock Trends (October 26): Trump again raises military action against Iran, AWS compute bookings extended to 2028

stories.summary: Brent crude fell about 1% to near $115 in Asia on Monday after jumping 6.2% last week to its highest weekly close in over four years, driven by Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. Trump said a strike on Iran would not happen on Sunday, and Qatari mediators were in Tehran. TechFlow notes there is still no clear plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz shipping.

explainer.meaning: when a central bank leaves rates unchanged but signals it is ready to raise them soon

stories.headline: Fed expected to hold on Wednesday, with markets pricing a December hike

impacts.why: FXStreet: inflation-driven Fed hike bets cap gold's upside ahead of the meeting.

stories.meaning: Wednesday at 6pm UK the Fed announces its decision. A hold is expected; what matters is whether it hints at a December rise. Higher US rates tend to weigh on gold and on expensive growth shares like tech.

priced_in.note: Hold ~90% priced (CME via TradingKey); December hike ~80% (Reuters).

sources.title: Asian shares make cautious start, Brent eases from six-month high
The Week Ahead: Fed rate decision looming as Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report earnings
Gold rebounds from three-month low, holds $4,000 as FOMC looms

stories.summary: The Fed is expected to keep rates at 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday after September's hike; CME FedWatch put a hold at about 90.6% as of 22 Oct. Reuters says markets price roughly an 80% chance of a hike in December, and Goldman Sachs expects one. There are no new projections at this meeting, so the statement and Chair Warsh's press conference are the focus.

explainer.meaning: the Fed's preferred measure of how fast US consumer prices are rising; 'core' leaves out food and energy

stories.headline: US Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation due Thursday
stories.meaning: These are the last big US data before markets decide on a December rate rise. Stronger numbers would make a hike more likely, which has recently weighed on gold and tech shares.

sources.title: Asian shares make cautious start, Brent eases from six-month high
The Week Ahead: Fed rate decision looming as Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report earnings

stories.summary: Preliminary Q3 GDP is forecast at a 3.2% annualised pace, helped by heavy data-centre spending, and core PCE inflation is expected to hold at 3.1%. Both are released on Thursday 29 Oct at 8:30am ET (12:30pm UK). TradingKey says strong growth and sticky core inflation could raise December hike expectations.

explainer.meaning: a UK government bond; its yield is what the government pays to borrow and feeds into mortgage rates

stories.headline: Pound steady near $1.335 ahead of Healey's first Budget on Wednesday
stories.meaning: Your ETFs are bought in pounds but mostly own overseas assets, so the pound's moves change their value in pounds. The Budget on Wednesday is the next possible trigger for the pound and UK borrowing costs.

priced_in.note: Sterling flat at $1.3346 (Reuters); options markets saw the Budget as a modest risk (Coming up).

sources.title: Asian shares make cautious start, Brent eases from six-month high

stories.summary: Sterling held at $1.3346 on Monday ahead of new Chancellor John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday, against a backdrop of rising borrowing costs and high energy prices. The Bank of England is not expected to move this week; JPMorgan's Bruce Kasman expects its first move next month. The 10-year US Treasury yield is about 5.0%, below its early-month peak of 5.36%.

topline: Amazon's Andy Jassy says AWS capacity is largely sold out through 2027 with some 2028 booked, days before Thursday's Q3 results.
Big week for your Mag7 pie: Alphabet reports Wednesday (consensus EPS $3.00) and Amazon Thursday (about $1.97), with AI spending under scrutiny.
Taiwan's regulator blocked Grab's Foodpanda Taiwan deal over Uber's 13.1% stake; Grab says its core Southeast Asian business is unaffected.
Gold is back just above $4,000 after a 4% weekly fall, and Brent oil eased about 1% from a four-year high on Iran headlines.
Wednesday also brings the Fed (hold expected, December hike ~80% priced) and the UK Budget; no new prices as markets were shut over the weekend.
